newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed tells Chechens he'll be Russian president.
newsitem.headline: Lebed tells Chechens he'll be Russian president.

text.p: Russia's former security chief Alexander Lebed took his presidential drive to rebel Chechnya on Wednesday and won a vote of confidence from the rebels Moscow had tried to crush.

"Everyone here, from the youngest to the oldest, wants you to become president of Russia," a traditionally-dressed Chechen man shouted to the gruff former paratroop general who stopped Russia's 21-month conflict with Chechnya last August.
"And I will," Lebed growled back, while the armed Chechens surrounding him raised their fists in salute and shouted their Moslem war cry "Allah Akhbah (God is greatest)".

He was speaking after the inauguration ceremony of Aslan Maskhadov, the breakaway region's president, who signed a peace deal with him last August paving the way for the withdrawal of Russian troops humiliated by the rebels.
The agreement also deferred by five years the issue at the heart of the conflict -- Chechnya's future political status.

Lebed's visit appeared aimed as much to promote his campaign to succeed President Boris Yeltsin in the Kremlin as to show support for the peace process he began before being removed last October as security chief for his overt presidential ambitions.

"Are Russian state television and Russian public television here? Right, you have the first questions," said his press secretary at the beginning of a news conference by Lebed after the inauguration ceremony.
"The system is rotting, soon it will fall apart," Lebed said, echoing his regular refrain about Russia's administration.
The soldier-turned-politician had little trouble winning the support of the rebels who had turned out in force for the cermony.
Asked about the prisoners-of-war still held by Russia he said they should be freed and added:

"They fought for their land. I would have done exactly the same in their place if someone had come to me to restore 'constitutional order' with air raids and howitzers," he said, to loud cheers from the Chechens in the audience.

Lebed also aired new pacifist credentials. "I've come to the conclusion that war is stupidity, it's a dead end, new graveyards...idiotism," he said, adding later that Russia should gradually get rid of its nuclear weapons.
But, asked repeatedly whether he would recognise Chechen independence if he became president, he side-stepped the question.
"We will sort out our relations, but with a cool head. Emotions must calm down," he said, with an eye to the millions outside Chechnya who would vote in a future Russian election.
Lebed finished a strong third in the first round of the presidential election in June and was immediately drafted by Yeltsin, helping him to win the run-off in July.
Yeltsin had a heart by-pass operation in November and suffered a pneumonia in January.
Lebed, whom most opinion polls call the most popular politician in Russia, says he has no doubt there will be an early presidential election which he will win.
